skill.name: async-python-patterns
skill.description: Guidance for building Python asyncio applications with async/await, concurrent I/O, task coordination, and non-blocking design patterns.
skill.summary: Build reliable async Python applications with practical asyncio patterns.
skill.author: wshobson

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown backticks, placeholder URLs, or benign sample identifiers. One semantic issue remains: the database example builds SQL with f-string interpolation, which may teach unsafe query construction if copied.

remediation.issue: Unsafe SQL interpolation in the async database example.
remediation.suggestion: Replace f-string SQL examples with parameterized queries and note that user input must never be concatenated into SQL.
Label example endpoints as placeholders and recommend mocks or controlled test services for tutorials and tests.

content.value_statement: Async Python code can stall when tasks, timeouts, and blocking calls are handled poorly. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code concrete asyncio patterns for reliable concurrent I/O.
actual_capabilities: Explains event loops, coroutines, tasks, futures, async context managers, and async iterators.
Provides examples for gather, create_task, timeouts, cancellation, and error handling.
Shows queues, semaphores, locks, connection pools, and batching patterns.
Covers async HTTP, database, WebSocket, and background task scenarios.
Lists common pitfalls such as missing await, blocking calls, and sync-async mixing.
limitations: It is a documentation skill, not a runnable library or framework.
Examples use simulated services and placeholder endpoints.
It does not replace review for database security, retries, or production observability.
It assumes working knowledge of Python functions, types, and basic I/O.

use_cases.title: Design Async API Handlers
use_cases.description: Plan FastAPI or aiohttp handlers that call databases and services concurrently with timeouts.

use_cases.title: Coordinate I/O Pipelines
use_cases.description: Process many independent I/O tasks in controlled batches without blocking the event loop.

use_cases.title: Review Async Reliability
use_cases.description: Check async code for cancellation, rate limits, task cleanup, and blocking operations.

prompt_templates.title: Convert Basic I/O
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner conversion from synchronous I/O to async style.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this synchronous Python I/O flow. Explain how to convert it to async/await using asyncio patterns from this skill.

prompt_templates.title: Add Timeouts And Errors
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate hardening for existing async functions.
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect this async Python function. Add timeout, cancellation, and exception handling guidance without changing the business behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Design Worker Queue
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced producer-consumer design for controlled concurrency.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an asyncio producer-consumer workflow for these tasks. Include queue sizing, worker lifecycle, backpressure, and graceful shutdown.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Production Flow
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review of a full async service path.
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this async service path for event loop blocking, unbounded concurrency, missing cleanup, and unsafe shared state. Prioritize fixes.

output_examples.input: I need to fetch five API resources concurrently.
output: Run the requests together with a bounded concurrency pattern.
Add request timeouts and collect failures separately from successful responses.

output_examples.input: My async service hangs under load.
output_examples.output: The review would look for blocking calls, missing timeouts, unbounded tasks, and cleanup paths that ignore cancellation.

output_examples.input: We need background workers for incoming jobs.
output: Use an asyncio queue for backpressure.
Cancel workers cleanly after the queue drains.

best_practices: Add timeouts and cancellation handling around slow I/O.
Use semaphores or queues to control concurrency.
Keep blocking CPU work or sync I/O outside the event loop.
anti_patterns: Calling blocking functions directly from async handlers.
Launching unbounded tasks for every item in a large collection.
Copying sample SQL strings into production without parameterized queries.

faq.question: Does this skill run async code for me?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and examples for writing async Python code.

faq.question: Which Python feature is the main focus?
faq.answer: The main focus is asyncio with async/await, tasks, queues, and coordination primitives.

faq.question: Can it help with FastAPI services?
faq.answer: Yes. It can guide async handler design, concurrent I/O, timeouts, and background work.

faq.question: Does it cover testing async code?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes pytest-asyncio examples and timeout testing patterns.

faq.question: Are the endpoints in examples production targets?
faq.answer: No. The URLs are placeholders or public test endpoints used for demonstration.

faq.question: What should I review before production use?
faq.answer: Review rate limits, retries, cancellation, database query safety, observability, and resource cleanup.
